question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $47u+20v=\text{gcd}(47,20).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}47 & = & 20\cdot 2 & + & 7 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 20 & = & 7\cdot 2 & + & 6 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 7 & = & 6\cdot 1 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(20,47)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}7 & =47-20\cdot 2 \\ 6 & =20-7\cdot 2 \\ 1 & =7-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =7-6 \\  & =7-(20-7\cdot 2) \\  & =7\cdot 3-20 \\  & =[47-20\cdot 2]\cdot 3-20 \\  & =47\cdot 3-20\cdot 7 \\  & =47\cdot 3+20\cdot (-7)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=3$ and $v=-7.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=3+(-7)=-4.
$$
